title: The payment provider's webhook
summary: How a request with no session authenticates itself by HMAC over raw bytes, how a duplicate or out-of-order delivery is neutralised, and the one thing it is allowed to change.
note: This whole flow is gated closed in a default build: cloudEnabled() reads VITAE_CLOUD_ENABLED, which .env.example:40 leaves false, and the handler returns 404 CLOUD_DISABLED before touching the body. Note also that the Cloud and Paddle variables are read straight from process.env in cloud/config.ts, not through the validated schema in packages/config/src/env.ts, so none of the boot-time production refusals cover them. The webhook is the only thing that changes what a workspace may do — a checkout creates a provider transaction and grants nothing, and returning from a checkout page proves nothing.

actors.label: Paddle
actors.note: The payment provider. Retries deliveries, and can deliver them out of order.

actors.label: POST /webhooks/paddle
actors.note: Registered at app.ts:50, above every JSON parser and above the auth gate. Reachable by position, not by any public-path declaration.

actors.label: cloud/paddle
actors.note: Signature verification, parsing, and the one transaction that applies an event.

actors.label: Control plane
actors.note: applyBillingAccess is the only writer of workspace access state from a provider event.

actors.label: errorHandler
actors.note: The handler catches and calls next(error), so every refusal leaves as the same envelope the rest of the API uses.

steps.label: POST /webhooks/paddle with header paddle-signature: ts=...;h1=...
steps.note: No session, no cookie, no bearer token. Possession of the shared secret is the authentication.

steps.label: 404 CLOUD_DISABLED before anything else is read
steps.note: A self-hosted install does not admit that the endpoint exists. This is the first check in the handler.

steps.label: take the untouched Buffer from express.raw (limit 1mb)
steps.note: Registered before every JSON parser deliberately: the signature covers the exact bytes sent, and parsing then re-serialising the object would change them and invalidate it.

steps.label: 401 INVALID_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE — no secret, stale timestamp, or digest mismatch
steps.note: Three ways to fail: the timestamp must be within five seconds of now; each candidate digest must be 64 hex characters of the right byte length before it is decoded, so malformed attacker input is a clean false rather than a timingSafeEqual length exception; and the comparison itself is constant time.

steps.label: 400 INVALID_WEBHOOK — not a Buffer, or no event_id/event_type after parsing
steps.note: Two separate checks: the body must be a raw Buffer (routes/webhooks/paddle.ts:13), and parsePaddleWebhook (cloud/paddle.ts:170) must find both an event_id and an event_type. Parsing happens only after the signature verified, so there is never a parsed object to be confused about.

steps.label: open one transaction; resolve custom_data.workspace_id against a real workspace
steps.note: The workspace id arrives inside the event's custom_data, which the server itself put on the transaction at checkout. It is confirmed to exist before it is used; an unknown id resolves to null rather than being trusted.

steps.label: INSERT the event on provider_event_id ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
steps.note: The unique provider event id is the idempotency key. This is the exactly-once boundary: a redelivery loses the insert race and never reaches the lifecycle transition.

steps.label: duplicate delivery: return early, change nothing
steps.note: Answered 200 with { duplicate: true } so the provider stops retrying. An event carrying no resolvable workspace is likewise stored as unlinked evidence, marked processed, and grants nothing.

steps.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on workspace_lifecycles to serialize this workspace's events
steps.note: The lifecycle row is locked first, not the subscription row: a durable lifecycle row exists for every workspace, whereas FOR UPDATE alone cannot lock the absent subscription row on a first subscription. That is what makes ordering hold under concurrent delivery as well as ordinary retries.

steps.label: compare the provider timestamp against the stored one; mark stale if older or absent
steps.note: The provider's own timestamp is the ordering key. Once one has been recorded, an older — or an entirely un-timestamped — retry can only be audit evidence; it must never roll a customer's entitlement backwards.

steps.label: not stale: upsert billing_customers and billing_subscriptions
steps.note: Status, billing period, current period end, cancel-at-period-end and the raw payload. Nothing about the plan's price comes from the event — the price catalogue is server-owned.

steps.label: applyBillingAccess(workspaceId, mapped access state)
steps.note: The whole permitted vocabulary: active, trialing, past_due, or read_only for canceled/cancelled/paused. A transaction.completed or transaction.paid event maps to active. Any other status maps to null and changes no access at all.

steps.label: update workspace_lifecycles; write a lifecycle event when the state actually changed
steps.note: This is the only thing the webhook is allowed to change. past_due gets a payment grace deadline; read_only gets an export grace deadline before deletion. A workspace with no lifecycle row is a silent no-op rather than a create.

steps.label: stamp processed_at, commit
steps.note: Storing the event, ordering it and transitioning access all commit together, so a crash mid-flight cannot leave an event recorded as processed without its effect.
